newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FORECAST-ANZ half profit seen stronger.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-ANZ half profit seen stronger.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) is seen posting a modest rise in half year earnings on Wednesday, in line with two other major Australian banks which reported this month, analysts said.

Analysts polled by Reuters estimated a net profit of between A$580 to A$630 million for the bank for the half year to March 31, a rise of between 11.5 percent to 21.2 percent over the bank's previous half result of A$520 million.
Forecasts for the bank's half year dividend payout ranged from 19 cents a share to 24 cents.

On May 15, Australia's largest bank, National Australia Bank Ltd recorded a 14 percent rise for the half while a day earlier, Westpac Banking Corp posted a 13 percent gain. Bank analyst at BNP Equities Linda Lyon said that like the other major banks, ANZ's earnings were likely to be negatively impacted by tigher margins in the home loan market.
"In theory, ANZ should have a higher proportion of business loans (than the other major banks) but it may not be higher than National Australia Bank (NAB)," Lyon said.
Lyon, who forecasted a half year net profit of about A$580 million, said that like NAB, ANZ's offshore operations should continue to show improvement.
Mike Pulman, ABN Amro Hoare Govett bank analyst said some abnormals would likely impact ANZ's net figure.
Pulman said these would likely include interest recovery from a dimissed claim against the bank's ANZ Grindlays unit in India and costs due to the restructure of the bank's Australian operations.
ANZ reported a six percent rise in net profit to A$1.12 billion for the year to September 30, 1996.
Analysts' full year projections ranged from A$1.188 billion to A$1.278 billion, representing a rise of between 6.1 percent and 14.1 percent.

Macquarie Equities bank analyst Graham Maloney forecast full year earnings of A$1.278 billion for the bank and said he was expecting a full-year abnormal gain of A$76 million, primarily due to the ANZ Grindlays settlement.

At the bank's annual meeting in January, ANZ's chairman, Charles Goode said the bank's first quarter performance was as expected, with falling interest margins offset by continued growth in lending assets and increased fee income.
Goode said ANZ expected to see tangible evidence of the benefits of the restructuring of its domestic banking businesses in Australia and New Zealand.
"We also expect to see higher profits flowing from the development of our international banking operations," he said.
ANZ shares closed 21.5 cents higher at A$8.53 on Monday.
